items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: we hired little John Jenkins on alto... So all of us Chicago guys were going to record... John Jenkins we got in the studio

ctx.x: Quartet. And that was my introduction to Thelonious, and with five of us Wilbur and I why, we'd hang out all during the week. And he said, "How come I never saw you when I came to Chicago?" Well, what could I tell him? This is Thelonious, the first time I ever meet the guy, and I'm standing in awe of this giant. But he was a beautiful person, you know? And I remember that well, because at the end of the week, he received a telegram from his wife saying his mother died, and wanted him to come home right away.

He says, "Well, "I left New York when mama was alive and I don't want to go back and see her in the casket and all that ..." because Sol had asked him to stay over an extra 2 nights to work with us, which he did. And the following week, here come -- we played behind Art Farmer -- Jody, and we hired little John Jenkins on alto, you know, and that went on - and anyway, I fooled around, and I didn't show up -- Drugs had something to do with that.
Well, how long did you keep that gig there?

items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: all of '58 I was recording with different people; Clifford Jordan, John Jenkins Jacob, Hank Mobley -- did a whole lot of dates with him

ctx.x: The period after you had gotten sick and the band broke up, you went back with Miles -- and then what did you do?

Well, I started working in gigs of my own -- maybe that was about '57 or '58, and all of '58 I was recording with different people; Clifford Jordan, John Jenkins Jacob, Hank Mobley -- did a whole lot of dates with him --

I was working out in Brooklyn with my own group, and I walked up on the gig, playing drums - Brooklyn - but before then I was working out of the Continental at a club with my own group; the picture on the back of the Chicago Sound, that was taken in that club by a fellow called [Selly] Copeland, he was a male nurse who just happened to take that photo And I think he sold it to Keepnews to put on the album. But anyway, I was working out there, and I used with Duke Jordan on piano and I forget who was on drums, to…
